discovery: Theoretical prediction and establishment of altermagnetism as a third fundamental class of collinear magnetic order

nominees.name: Tomas Jungwirth
nominees.affiliation: Institute of Physics, Czech Academy of Sciences, Prague; University of Nottingham

nominees.name: Libor Šmejkal
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute for the Physics of Complex Systems, Dresden; Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz

motivation: Using spin-group symmetry analysis, Šmejkal, Sinova and Jungwirth showed that collinear magnets fall into three distinct classes, not two. Altermagnets have zero net magnetization, like antiferromagnets, yet their bands carry alternating, momentum-dependent spin splitting of nonrelativistic origin, as ferromagnets do. This is an organizing principle derived from symmetry, and it transforms our understanding of magnetic order. It predicted concrete material candidates, including RuO2, MnTe and CrSb, and an anomalous Hall effect without net moment. Angle-resolved photoemission and imaging experiments in 2024 confirmed altermagnetic band splitting directly, and several independent groups reproduced the results. The concept connects magnetism, unconventional superconductivity and topology, and it offers a route to fast, stray-field-free spintronics. Theory arriving first and rigorous experimental verification following is the kind of advance the Nobel Prize should honour.
